title: a post Instagram rejected is marked failed with no retry and no alarm -- the slot is lost silently
evidence: 1 post(s) marked failed in the last 24h (newest 4.7h ago): post 333 photo 339 slot 2026-09-20 15:15:13.541039 failed 2026-09-20 16:00:58.718029 reason: instagram: 400 code 9007 (Media ID is not available -- the media is not ready for publishing); backfilled 2026-09-20 from log/scheduled_posting.log (row predates failure_reason). packs/scheduling/lib/tasks/scheduled_posting.rake calls record_failure! with no requeue (the row's failure_reason carries the cause; rows written before 2026-09-20 have none, so grep the post id in log/scheduled_posting.log for those). Nothing else can see it: check_publish_liveness counts only scheduled/draft rows past due, and check_publish_gap measures the newest POSTED post. Known cause: Instagram 400 code 9007 'media not ready for publishing'. Suggested fix -- one bounded retry on 9007 -- changes live publish behaviour, so it is Tim's call.

notes.note: 2026-09-20 16:5xZ ops-triage: DETECTION half FIXED in-repo; the retry half is Tim's call. Root cause of the invisibility: the class is 'a row with status=failed', and every publish check looked elsewhere -- check_publish_liveness counts only scheduled/draft rows past due, check_publish_gap measures the newest POSTED post -- so a rejected post was unobservable while its slot was permanently lost. Added check_publish_failed_silent + pure publish_failed_verdict to bin/tc_ops.py: it counts scheduling_posts with status='failed' and updated_at inside PUBLISH_FAILED_WINDOW_H (24h) and files this key with the post/photo/slot and the known cause. VERIFIED live: probe fires it on today's real failure -- '1 post(s) marked failed in the last 24h (newest 0.7h ago): post 333 photo 339 slot 2026-09-20 15:15:13 failed 2026-09-20 16:00:58'; selftest 129 assertions / 0 failures (4 new verdict cases); psql cross-check: exactly 1 failed row in 24h, 65 lifetime, so the check is quiet on history and loud on a live loss. The record is now PROBE-OWNED (source manual -> probe) so it auto-closes when no rejection falls in the window instead of staying open forever; the 24h window is what makes that correct. NOT fixed, deliberately: the lost slot itself. scheduled_posting.rake:121-125 calls mark_as_failed! with no requeue, and the suggested one-bounded-retry on Instagram code 9007 (container-readiness race) changes live publish behaviour -- the same class of edit Tim reserved -- so it is filed as a decision, not applied. Also proposed: persist the failure reason (the row stores none; it survives only in log/scheduled_posting.log).

2026-09-20 19:4xZ ops-triage: the TRANSIENT half of the no-retry defect is now FIXED in-repo (commit ffe9692). Root cause of the 9007 class: Instagram answers the container status check status_code=FINISHED, then rejects the immediate publish with 400 code 9007/subcode 2207027 'media is not ready for publishing'; the client published with no tolerance and the publisher has no requeue, so the slot AND its photo were lost. Instagram::Client now classifies that response (MediaNotReadyError) and retries the publish 4x, 10s apart; every other error and the last attempt fail exactly as before. Verified: spec/services/scheduling/instagram_client_spec.rb is RED on the unfixed client (2 failures) and green after; full suite 409 examples / 0 failures; adjacent specs green. REMAINING (needs Tim): a post that definitively fails still consumes its slot with no requeue -- is a missed slot made up, or dropped? That is a product policy call, not a code defect.

Residual is product policy, not code: a post that definitively fails still consumes its slot with no requeue -- make-up the slot, or drop it? Tim's call.
